svg.title: 420 physical messages for 60 logical sends, without dedup -- exactly 60 with it
svg.desc: A producer sends 60 logical messages under an absurdly tight request.timeout.ms, causing repeated retries even though the broker is actually succeeding within its real replication time. Without enable.idempotence, the topic receives 420 physical messages for 60 logical sends -- every retry becomes a real duplicate, invisible to the application since every delivery callback still reports success. With enable.idempotence=True, the broker tracks a producer ID and per-partition sequence number for every message, recognizes each retry as a repeat of one already appended, and the topic ends up with exactly 60 messages -- an exact match, every run.
svg.text: Same 60 Sends, Same Tight Timeout, Opposite Result on the Topic
WITHOUT enable.idempotence
request.timeout.ms=1 -- gives up before the ack arrives
60 delivery callbacks: all report success
broker has no way to recognize a retry as a repeat
420 messages
landed on the topic, for 60 logical sends
a different run measured 540 instead --
always dramatically more than 60
WITH enable.idempotence=True
identical timeout, identical retries
producer ID + per-partition sequence number
on every message, checked by the broker
60 messages
landed on the topic, for 60 logical sends
every retry recognized and dropped --
an exact match, every single run
enable.idempotence prevents duplicate writes from producer retries -- nothing more
It says nothing about consumer-side processing, which is still governed by the commit-timing
choice Lesson 1 proved directly -- "idempotent" here means the write path only.
